items.title: In-venue watch parties: An affordable pathway to fandom
items.summary: During this year's Stanley Cup Final the Carolina Hurricanes opened their arena for all three road games, showing the away game on the video board for $10 admission with free parking, and at least two of the three sold out. The column cites a YouGov Sport poll of 1,007 US sports fans in which 51% said they would attend an in-arena watch party for a team they follow, with interest highest for championship series and lowest for regular-season games. It notes low ticket price leads the reasons for demand at 41% and links the idea to earlier YouGov data showing 86% of US fans feel live sport is becoming a luxury.
items.what_it_means: Teams can sell the shared live experience at a low price point even when the game itself is elsewhere, opening the building to fans priced out of real tickets.

items.title: Brewers Raking in Cash From World Series Run
items.summary: The Brewers' first World Series in more than 40 years has produced league records for merchandise, including the highest total postseason sales and the most sales in the 48 hours after a pennant clinch, plus a single-day in-venue franchise record during Game 1. Resale get-in prices in Milwaukee set a World Series record for Game 1 and stayed above $2,000 for Game 2, while prices for the Rays' home games in Tampa Bay are falling. The piece notes the Brewers' fan base regularly outperforms MLB's smallest media market.
items.what_it_means: A rare big moment can unlock spending from a whole region far beyond what the market size would predict, and the contrast with Tampa shows demand is not automatic.

items.title: NBA adds Kalshi, Polymarket as sponsors and sets integrity framework
items.summary: The NBA unveiled a framework naming Kalshi and Polymarket as preferred prediction market exchanges and league sponsors, with logo use and promotional rights, and allowing other prediction operators to advertise during games and sponsor teams. The deal includes safeguards such as official Sportradar data, limits on markets the league sees as vulnerable to manipulation and an information-sharing agreement with the CFTC. It could also open sponsorship deals for the 14 teams in states without legal online sports betting. Financial terms were not disclosed.
items.what_it_means: A new sponsorship category has opened across the league and its teams, including markets that sports betting could not reach.

items.title: Allianz secures naming rights to LA28 venue
items.summary: Allianz has secured naming rights to Allianz Beach Arena, a temporary venue of nearly 15,000 seats in Long Beach that will host beach volleyball at the LA28 Olympics and blind soccer at the Paralympics. LA28 is the first organising committee allowed to sell venue naming rights, under an IOC pilot, and only one other temporary venue has been sold so far. Terms were not disclosed, though LA28's chairman has previously put the price at nine figures, varying by venue. Allianz already names seven venues worldwide.
items.what_it_means: The Olympics has created a new naming-rights inventory for temporary venues, testing what a short-lived name is worth to a global sponsor.

items.title: Italian club Venezia FC using fashion to boost global attention
items.publication: Sports Business Journal (citing The New York Times)
items.summary: Serie A club Venezia FC's American owners have run a branding push to take the club beyond its modest local audience and volatile results, including a redesigned visual identity by Bureau Borsche and a kit worn by influencers, models and celebrities. The club's revenue chief describes the aim as tying the team as closely as possible to the city of Venice. The report notes many clubs are recasting themselves as fashion brands, but Venezia stands out because it was not a famous club, and it currently sits last in Serie A.
items.what_it_means: A small club is borrowing a city's global fame to reach people who will never watch a match, with brand and merch revenue that does not depend on results.

items.title: Ariat Arena: Fort Worth's Dickies Arena Gets New Name In New Naming Rights Partnership
items.summary: Fort Worth's 14,000-capacity Dickies Arena, home of the Fort Worth Stock Show and Rodeo, has been renamed Ariat Arena under a 10-year naming rights deal with the Western workwear brand, effective immediately. Ariat becomes the venue's exclusive partner for Western wear, work wear and boots, and was already a longstanding corporate partner of the Stock Show and Rodeo. Terms were not disclosed, and the deal includes a charitable giving programme for Fort Worth-area organisations.
items.what_it_means: A naming-rights swap between two brands in the same category shows how closely venue names are tied to the audience a building already draws.

items.title: Brewers fans bought more than 30,000 'Racing Sausages' in first two World Series games
items.summary: Fans at American Family Field bought more than 300,000 food and beverage items in World Series Games 1 and 2, nearly four per person, according to provider Delaware North, including more than 30,000 Racing Sausages. Delaware North also sold about 3,000 postseason specialty items and four times its NLCS souvenir numbers. It says planning for a postseason run starts about three months out.
items.what_it_means: Per-head spend on food, drink and souvenirs jumps sharply at big moments, and venues that plan ahead capture it.

items.title: DirecTV adds NHL team channels in multiyear deal
items.summary: DirecTV reached a multiyear deal to carry four NHL team-run channels, including the Blues' Blue Note+, for subscribers in each team's home territory, along with rights for bars, restaurants and other commercial venues in those regions. The deal ends a negotiation that ran into the season and left many St. Louis fans unable to watch the Blues. DirecTV now has local rights for 76 of the 81 US-based NHL, NBA and MLB teams.
items.what_it_means: Team-owned channels still depend on pay-TV distribution to reach fans, and gaps during negotiations cost teams visibility in season.

items.title: PLL sets viewership, attendance records during 2026 season
items.summary: The Premier Lacrosse League had its most-watched and most-attended season, with average viewership up 22% year over year to 265,000 and a single-game record of 612,000 on ABC. It reported 10 sold-out events across five markets, social video views up 56% across PLL and Women's Lacrosse League channels, and onsite merchandise sales up 11%.
items.what_it_means: A touring league model is growing audiences across TV, social and live at once for a niche sport.

items.title: Garth Brooks Pauses KC Onsale After Bot Swarm
items.summary: Garth Brooks' team paused ticket sales for an added Kansas City matinee after what it called excessive bot activity, with Brooks posting that the bot situation is out of hand and has been getting worse on the tour. Every ticket on the tour is the same $155 all-in price, part of his long-running approach to fighting bots and the secondary market, which includes adding shows until demand is met.
items.what_it_means: Flat pricing and extra dates do not stop bots on their own, and failed onsales damage the relationship with the fans who did buy.
